source.title: Stable ResNet
source.authors: Soufiane Hayou; Eugenio Clerico; Bo He; George Deligiannidis; A. Doucet; J. Rousseau

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test accuracy for scaled and unscaled ResNets, but no training classification error or other result that tests the listed claim versions. Its training results concern test accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports trained ResNet test accuracies in Tables 3 and 4; these do not measure the training-error behavior in the claim versions. Tables 1 and 2 report NNGP kernel predictor test accuracy, not gradient-based training. Theoretical gradient and kernel results are not training-error results.
record.test_reason: The study proves gradient and kernel properties of scaled residual networks and reports kernel-predictor and trained-network test accuracy. It does not measure training error, local-minimum frequency, learning speed, trainable depth in plain networks, stability-threshold dynamics, or BatchNorm learning-rate tolerance. Its gradient-at-initialization results concern residual networks and do not directly test V4's plain-network claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that stable residual scaling controls gradients, preserves infinite-depth expressivity, makes NNGP inference robust and improves SGD-trained ResNet test accuracy; optimal scaling remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces layer/depth-dependent scaling of residual blocks; reports test accuracy rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracies vary with dataset, depth, scaling type, and BatchNorm condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Every scaled variant in Tables 3 and 4 has higher reported mean test accuracy than its corresponding unscaled baseline. The record's claimed below-baseline exceptions are incorrect. Decreasing scaling does not consistently outperform uniform scaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-block scaling improves reported test accuracy in these trained ResNet experiments, with gains depending on dataset, depth, normalization and scaling choice.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 1 establishes a depth-independent gradient second-moment bound for square-summable residual scalings and exponential growth under uniformly positive scalings, under its infinite-width and loss assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-dependent residual scaling can control gradients at initialization in infinitely wide ReLU residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The limiting NNGP and NTK kernels retain universality under stable scaling, subject to the stated bias and input-domain conditions. These are expressivity results rather than measured optimization outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stable residual scaling preserves kernel expressivity in the infinite-depth limit.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2021)
record.problems: For trained ResNet experiments, only test accuracy is reported, so the results do not establish whether training error approaches zero. The authors report 3 independent runs and test-accuracy error intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from Tables 3 and 4. Tables 1 and 2 are omitted because they report NNGP kernel predictor test accuracy, not outcomes of gradient-based training.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including corrupted or random labels and model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Two-layer teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks; special plain-network initializations and Fixup.
Learning speed and trainable depth of plain networks under activation-matched initialization, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature and sharpness trajectories, and divergence.
Accuracy gained over training time and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BatchNorm; Fixup training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix A7.2 reports best test accuracy and error intervals from three repetitions. Final or selected test accuracy cannot establish training speed or near-zero training error. BatchNorm and non-BatchNorm experiments also use different batch sizes and learning-rate selection procedures. None of the own-method comparisons supplies a verdict on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training error, label corruption, random labels, model size, optimizer, and stopping.
Teacher-student local minima and student width.
Training error by depth, plain networks versus identity shortcuts, and comparisons to the cited special initializations.
Training speed and trainable depth under initialization variants.
Training dynamics above a stability limit, loss and sharpness trajectories, and divergence.
Accuracy gained during training and learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization.
